auth_context_files.purpose: Legacy auth context returned by withAuth(), requireAuth(), etc.

canonical_auth_context_files.definition: { verifiedActorId, verifiedActorType, verifiedActor, verifiedWorkspaceId, verifiedCapabilities, traceId, executionTrace, verifiedSessionSnapshot, correlationId, requestId, request, session?, policy? }
canonical_auth_context_files.purpose: New verified context passed to route handlers

wrapper_return_types.notes: Throws if auth fails, returns AuthContext
Throws if capability missing, returns AuthContext
Returns null if not authenticated (optional auth)
New wrapper, handler receives CanonicalAuthContext directly

bridge_gap_analysis.problem: AuthContext lacks: verifiedActorId, verifiedActorType, verifiedWorkspaceId, verifiedCapabilities, traceId, executionTrace, verifiedSessionSnapshot, correlationId, requestId, request
bridge_gap_analysis.why_gap_exists: AuthContext is minimal (session + policy). CanonicalAuthContext is verified superset with execution context. withAuth() routes cannot produce CanonicalAuthContext without additional verified data.
bridge_gap_analysis.conversion_feasibility: POSSIBLE - AuthContext contains SessionInfo and PolicyContext, which can be converted to CanonicalAuthContext fields IF we have traceId, workspaceId, request context (all available at route level)
bridge_gap_analysis.prerequisite: Routes must pass request, workspace context, and trace context to converter

notes: AuthContext is returned by legacy auth functions in auth-guard.ts
CanonicalAuthContext is the new verified context standard
No existing converter between the two types
Routes using withAuth() cannot call these services without conversion
Bridge must convert without fabricating permissions or weakening enforcement
